meta_review.summary: This paper introduces a novel adversarial patch attack, termed Embedding Disruption Patch Attack (EDPA), specifically designed to target Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. The core idea behind EDPA is to disrupt the alignment between visual and textual embeddings within the VLA model by maximizing the discrepancy between the latent representations of clean and adversarially perturbed visual inputs. This is achieved by crafting a patch that, when applied to the visual input, causes the model to misinterpret the scene and generate incorrect actions. The authors emphasize that EDPA is model-agnostic, requiring no prior knowledge of the model's architecture, action space, or the specific robotic manipulator being used, making it a versatile attack method. The paper also proposes a corresponding defense mechanism, which involves adversarial fine-tuning of the visual encoder. This fine-tuning process aims to enhance the robustness of the VLA model against EDPA by training the encoder to be less sensitive to adversarial perturbations in the visual input. The authors conduct extensive experiments on the LIBERO robotic simulation benchmark to evaluate both the effectiveness of the EDPA attack and the robustness of the proposed defense. The results demonstrate that EDPA significantly increases the task failure rates of VLA models, while the adversarial fine-tuning effectively mitigates this effect, improving the model's resilience to the attack. The paper's primary contribution lies in the introduction of a model-agnostic adversarial patch attack for VLA models and a corresponding defense strategy, along with empirical validation of these methods on a robotic simulation benchmark. The findings highlight the vulnerability of VLA models to adversarial attacks and underscore the importance of developing robust defense mechanisms to ensure their reliable operation in real-world scenarios. The authors also provide a detailed analysis of the generated adversarial patches, noting their structural patterns reminiscent of robotic arms, which offers insights into the nature of the adversarial perturbations that VLA models are susceptible to. Overall, this work makes a significant contribution to the field by addressing the critical issue of adversarial robustness in VLA models, which are increasingly being deployed in safety-critical applications.
